pr_title: Improve parameter naming and documentation in `GraphEdit` and `GraphNode`
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/37227.
Supersedes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/40043.

This PR revives the aforementioned PR and improves on it. I've tried to clean up the language and introduce some consistency to the terms slots and ports. Slots are child controls, ports are their left and right connection acceptors. As such, `GraphEdit` doesn't work with slots, it only works with ports and their connections.

Like the original PR I've added a method to retrieve the slot index from the port, but it's actually two methods to keep in sync with the rest of the API for similar things. I've also renamed some internals for consistency and clarity. But the most important part for the users is the improvements to the documentation. Parameters should now have clear names respecting their quality without any mix-ups, and the descriptions have been tuned up.

I think this should reduce the confusion around slots and ports to the minimum without breaking any compatibility. (So it can be backported to 3.x if anyone is willing).
pr_comments:
Looks good can you help me write a summary?

> The GraphEdit class documentation uses the terms port and slot interchangeably to refer only to slots that are enabled,
whereas the GraphNode class documentation uses slot to refer to any slot, regardless of whether it is enabled or not.

What is the revised statement here?

@fire Now GraphEdit uses only the term port because that's what it works with. It was always ports, it was just mislabeled in a lot of cases. GraphNode, in turn, uses both terms, where slot is the "row" added by the child control and "port" is one of the slot's two connection dots.

This is also now explicitly explained in the GraphNode's description.

issue_context.title: Graph node confusing slot indexing
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:** 3.2.1

**OS/device including version:** Windows 10

**Issue description:**
It's not actually bug, but some confusing slot indexing. Real slot and connection slot have different indexing. Real slot index it's node index inside GraphNode, but connection slot index start from 0 and considers only active slot (enabled connection)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1756388/77249678-7948a980-6c75-11ea-9b68-0dd5c7a8c283.png)

**Example 1:**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1756388/77249799-3935f680-6c76-11ea-8a5b-f0f4d186e6e9.png)
_Connection request from node 'Node0' from slot '0' to node 'Node1' to slot '0'_

**Example 2:**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1756388/77249832-5b2f7900-6c76-11ea-94a6-17c4d6863862.png)
_Connection request from node 'Node1' from slot '0' to node 'Node0' to slot '1'_
comments:
I guess the fact that "slots" are referred as "ports" in some cases is related to this. It would make sense, that a "slot" is an inner concept for a `GraphNode` and a "port" is an external representation for active slot, as perceived by `GraphEdit`. But there is no way to convert one to the other. And it is still not consistent, as `connection_request` signal calls them "slots", while `connect_node` method calls them "ports".
```
connection_request ( String from, int from_slot, String to, int to_slot )
```
```
connect_node ( String from, int from_port, String to, int to_port )
```

Personally I would always refer to the slot as the index for the node being referred to, not the number of slots active on that side. 

- Since it currently refers to the number of slots that are enabled for connection, enabling a slot changes the index of all the slots below it.
- Since there is no built in way to retrieve the node that a slot refers to, you are currently can't do anything with the slot number

Right now I am getting around this by turning all slots on, but coloring them as transparent and setting their type numbers to -1 on the left and -2 on the right so they can't be connected to anything. This is SUPER hacky, but it makes the nodes function as expected.

> Right now I am getting around this by turning all slots on, but coloring them as transparent and setting their type numbers to -1 on the left and -2 on the right so they can't be connected to anything. This is SUPER hacky, but it makes the nodes function as expected.

Nice hack :D

>Since there is no built in way to retrieve the node that a slot refers to, you are currently can't do anything with the slot number

I tried replace `vector<ConnCache>` to `map<int, ConnCache>` to store slot index like key. This worked as expected for my code, but broke visual scripting logic and I think visual shader too. Easy way it's add new property `int slot` to `struct ConnCache` and methods to get slot index by port index.

To summarize, would the following changes suffice?

1. Add a function to `GraphNode` to get the slot index from the port/connection index
2. Modify `GraphEdit` class documentation to clarify difference between ports and slots, and change any ambiguous method/signal argument names

This would be the least disruptive and non-compatibility breaking change. If that sounds good, I can make a PR soon
I would feel that solves the problem.
